Build a rating-scale diagnostics report

Source: R/api-tables.R
rating_scale_table.Rd

Build a rating-scale diagnostics report

Usage 

rating_scale_table(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  whexact = FALSE,
  drop_unused = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional matching output from diagnose_mfrm(). Stored step uncertainty and marginal-fit results are reused when supplied. Without diagnostics, only observed/plug-in category statistics and step points are calculated; no covariance or full diagnostic calculation is started.

whexact

Retained for call compatibility. Category ZSTD is unavailable because grouping by the observed category changes its reference distribution.

drop_unused

If TRUE, remove categories with zero count from the displayed category table. Usage totals still cover the full declared scale; unavailable counts remain visible, and score-support caveats are retained.

Value

A named list with:

  • category_table: counts, generating measures and descriptive residuals. AvgMeasure is the observed-category average oriented predictor; ExpectedMeasure weights all predictors by their category probabilities. AvgPersonMeasure and ExpectedAverage retain distinct Person-only and predicted-score summaries. Category ZSTD and fit flags are NA: selecting by observed outcome destroys the universal unit-residual baseline.

  • owner_category_table: unfiltered counts within each step owner

  • model_context: model, estimator, step/slope owners and step scale

  • notes: interpretation outside the figure

  • threshold_table: model step/threshold estimates and stored uncertainty

  • summary: one-row summary with available/unavailable category counts and adjacent-threshold comparisons. Category-fit means identify their available denominators and describe displayed rows. Missing fit statistics/flags stay NA, including unused categories with no estimable category fit.

  • category_usage: counts across the full scale, before drop_unused

  • threshold_coverage: available, unavailable and decreasing adjacent-pair counts; NotApplicable distinguishes binary scales from missing estimates

  • caveats: structured score-support warning/review rows

  • diagnostic_mode: character scalar carried from diagnostics$diagnostic_mode ("legacy", "both", or "marginal_fit"); used by downstream reporting helpers to pick the correct expected-count basis

  • marginal_fit: list bundle from diagnostics$marginal_fit when strict marginal fit was computed, otherwise NULL. Carries the raw OverallRMSD / OverallMaxAbsStdResidual / per-cell tables that feed the MarginalOverallRMSD columns in summary.

Details

This helper provides category usage/fit statistics and threshold summaries for reviewing score-category functioning. category_table is a global observed-score screen. owner_category_table retains every declared category within each level of the fitted step_facet (or one Common family for RSM). Its percentages use that owner's total weight. These are observed ratings, not independent Persons or planned assignments. Missing categories alone cannot establish structural absence. drop_unused only filters the global display; owner counts stay complete.

Typical checks:

  • sparse category usage (Count, ExpectedCount)

  • category fit (Infit, Outfit, ZStd)

  • threshold ordering within each StepFacet (threshold_table$Estimate, GapFromPrev)

Interpreting output

Start with summary:

  • UsedCategories close to total Categories suggests that most score categories are represented in the observed data.

  • very small MinCategoryCount indicates potential instability.

  • ThresholdMonotonic = FALSE indicates disordered thresholds within at least one threshold set. In PCM fits, inspect threshold_table by StepFacet before drawing scale-wide conclusions.

Then inspect:

  • category_table for global category-level misfit/sparsity.

  • threshold_table for adjacent-step gaps and ordering within each StepFacet.

Stored diagnostics$parameter_uncertainty$steps are matched by threshold family and step, with fitted estimates and source identity checked. Inspect SE_Status, CIEligible, CIUse and UncertaintySourceStatus. Missing rows remain unavailable; duplicate or mismatched keys are rejected. Older diagnostics without a verifiable fitted-calibration identity must be regenerated with diagnose_mfrm(fit, ...); model refitting is not required. Reordering stored step rows does not change their keyed correspondence. A bare fit supplies step points with SE_Status = "not_supplied". A binary centered step has no free within-owner contrast (fixed_by_step_centering).

Native thresholds here are centered step offsets. They are not full ability-axis crossings, cumulative-50% boundaries or decision cuts. An SE for a step does not include the covariance required for a crossing or an adjacent-step difference. Threshold disorder is descriptive, not an automatic category-merging rule. Two-family GPCM diagnostics remain unsupported by this helper; use its dedicated response/curve routes.

Typical workflow

  1. Fit model: fit_mfrm().

  2. Build diagnostics: diagnose_mfrm().

  3. Run rating_scale_table() and review summary().

  4. Use plot() to visualize category profile quickly.

Save the complete result to retain owner counts, uncertainty status and notes. plot(out, type = "counts") shows global counts; use plot(out, type = "thresholds") for the stored step points. Both support as_ggplot() without recalculating values. Step figures do not draw stored SEs as crossing, gap or curve intervals; inspect threshold_table separately.

Further guidance

For a plot-selection guide and a longer walkthrough, see mfrmr_visual_diagnostics and vignette("mfrmr-visual-diagnostics", package = "mfrmr").

Output columns

The category_table data.frame contains:

Category

Score category value.

Count, Percent

Observed count and percentage of total. With observation weights, counts are sums of weights, not independent sample sizes. Missing or invalid scores/weights make the usage counts unavailable.

AvgMeasure, ExpectedMeasure

Observed-category mean oriented predictor and its model expectation, weighted by category probabilities across all retained observations.

AvgPersonMeasure

Mean person measure for respondents in this category; distinct from the oriented predictor.

ExpectedAverage

Mean predicted score among observations in this observed category; distinct from the expected generating measure.

Infit, Outfit

Descriptive category residual mean squares.

InfitZSTD, OutfitZSTD

Unavailable (NA); conditioning on the observed category does not preserve a universal unit-residual reference.

ExpectedCount, DiffCount

Expected count and observed-expected difference.

LowCount

Logical; TRUE if count is below minimum threshold.

InfitFlag, OutfitFlag, ZSTDFlag

Unavailable (NA). Outcome-selected residual summaries do not have a universal unit baseline or calibrated ZSTD reference. Low-count and generating-measure warnings remain descriptive.

ZeroCount, UnusedCategoryType, WeaklyIdentified, CategoryCaveat

Structured score-support caveats for retained zero-count categories.

The owner_category_table contains StepOwner (facet name), StepFacet (level), Category (model score), CategoryLabel (original score), raw and weighted counts (RawCount, Count), denominators (OwnerRatings, OwnerWeight), Percent, ZeroCount and UsageStatus. Status distinguishes observed, not observed, zero weight, no exposure and unavailable counts. No-exposure counts are zero but percentages are unavailable.

The threshold_table data.frame contains:

Step

Step label (e.g., Step_1, Step_2). Use LowerCategory and UpperCategory to identify the corresponding score transition.

Estimate

Estimated threshold/step difficulty (logits).

StepOwner

Name of the facet owning the steps, or Common for RSM.

StepFacet

Threshold family identifier when the fit uses facet-specific threshold sets.

SE, CI_Lower, CI_Upper, SE_Status, CIEligible, CIUse

Stored step uncertainty and reporting status, without new inference.

LowerCategoryLabel, UpperCategoryLabel

Original scores at the transition.

LowerOwnerCount, UpperOwnerCount, OwnerSupportStatus

Weighted counts and support within this threshold owner, not pooled frequencies.

GapFromPrev

Difference between adjacent numbered thresholds within the same StepFacet. Missing thresholds are not skipped to form a gap. No automatic category-merging rule is applied.

ThresholdMonotonic

Logical flag repeated within each threshold set. FALSE records at least one decreasing adjacent pair; TRUE requires every expected pair to be available and nondecreasing, allowing numerical differences up to sqrt(.Machine$double.eps). Equal thresholds meet this descriptive condition. Otherwise the flag is NA. A binary scale has only one threshold and no applicable ordering comparison. This is a statement about point estimates, not a test of category adequacy.

LowerCategory, UpperCategory, WeaklyIdentified, ThresholdCaveat

Adjacent score-category support metadata. Thresholds adjacent to retained zero-count categories are flagged for cautious interpretation.

References

  • Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43(4), 561-573. doi:10.1007/BF02293814

  • Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174. doi:10.1007/BF02296272

  • Linacre, J. M. (2002). What do Infit and Outfit, mean-square and standardized mean? Rasch Measurement Transactions, 16(2), 878. (Source for the 0.5-1.5 mean-square heuristic review interval; this is not a source for threshold-gap rules.)

  • Wind, S. A. (2023). Detecting rating scale malfunctioning with the partial credit model and generalized partial credit model. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 83(5), 953-983. doi:10.1177/00131644221116292 (Recent simulation evidence on PCM- and GPCM-based rating-scale diagnostics; useful for interpreting the summary(t8)$summary flags in the GPCM route.)

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), measurable_summary_table(), plot.mfrm_fit(), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples 

library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Review category use and the fitted transitions between scores
categories <- rating_scale_table(fit)
review <- summary(categories)
review$summary
#>   Categories DisplayedCategories AvailableCategoryCounts
#> 1          4                   4                       4
#>   UnavailableCategoryCounts UsedCategories UnusedScoreCategories
#> 1                         0              4                      
#>   WeaklyIdentifiedThresholds MinCategoryCount MaxCategoryCount
#> 1                          0               46               96
#>   MeanCategoryInfit AvailableCategoryInfit MeanCategoryOutfit
#> 1          1.079498                      4          0.9991048
#>   AvailableCategoryOutfit ThresholdMonotonic ThresholdComparisons
#> 1                       4               TRUE                    2
#>   AvailableThresholdComparisons UnavailableThresholdComparisons
#> 1                             2                               0
#>   ThresholdOrderNotApplicable DiagnosticMode ExpectedCountBasis
#> 1                       FALSE         legacy      legacy_plugin
#>   MarginalFitAvailable MarginalOverallRMSD MarginalMaxAbsStdResidual
#> 1                FALSE                  NA                        NA
#>   MarginalFlaggedCategories MarginalClassifiedCategories
#> 1                        NA                            0
#>   MarginalUnclassifiedCategories
#> 1                              0
categories$model_context
#>   Model Method StepOwner  StepSelection SlopeOwner            StepScale
#> 1   RSM    MML    Common not_applicable            centered_step_offset
head(categories$owner_category_table)

plot(categories)
